title: KV cache reuse, eviction, paging & memory-bandwidth investigation
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the investigation into KV cache behavior observed on the latest serving-runtime builds (main @ PR 612) with focus on reuse rates, eviction patterns, paging events, and host GPU memory bandwidth. Goal: identify dominant causes of higher-than-expected per-token latency and degraded throughput for long-chat workloads, and propose mitigations (policy/algorithmic and infra).

Background / motivation:
- Multiple customer and internal benchmarks (large-chat workloads; seq_len 2k-6k; batch sizes 1-8) started showing higher p99 latency and lower throughput compared to last quarter.
- Hypothesis: KV cache misses + eviction-induced paging are causing extra PCIe transfers and memory bandwidth contention, increasing token generation time.
- Investigation scope: model-agnostic profiling on A100 and L4 (to capture both HBM and GPU memory constrained cases).

Experiment setup:
- Code: serving-runtime main + PR 612 (kv-cache refactor)
- Models: redwood/med-7b (JIT-compiled kernel path) and open/llama-like 13B quantized 4-bit variant
- Hardware: AWS p4d (A100) and custom nodes with L4; host OS perf + nvidia-smi dmon + NVIDIA Nsight Systems traces for GPU-side metrics.
- Workloads: two traces from prod-sim harness: "chat-long-context" (avg seq 3.6k, highly conversational prefixes) and "assistant-search" (shorter, repeated prompts). Each run 30 min steady-state.
- Metrics captured: KV reuse rate (how often KV entries read vs regenerated), eviction rate (eviction ops / sec), page faults/paging events (host <-> GPU), GPU memory bandwidth (GB/s), per-token latency (ms), throughput (tokens/s).

Key measurements (steady-state aggregated, avg over 10 run windows):
- KV reuse rate:
  - chat-long-context: 54% reuse (A100), 47% reuse (L4)
  - assistant-search: 86% reuse (A100), 82% reuse (L4)
- Eviction rate (evictions / minute):
  - chat-long-context: 420 evictions/min (A100), 850 evictions/min (L4)
  - assistant-search: 40 evictions/min (A100), 60 evictions/min (L4)
- Paging events (host <-> GPU transfers per minute):
  - chat-long-context: 120 pci transfers/min (A100), 320 pci transfers/min (L4)
  - assistant-search: 12 pci transfers/min (A100), 18 pci transfers/min (L4)
- Observed GPU memory bandwidth (sustained during token generation):
  - chat-long-context: 250 GB/s average (A100 peak 310 GB/s), bursts to 420 GB/s during eviction+paging spikes
  - L4: 110 GB/s average, bursts to 190 GB/s
- Per-token latency impact (p50/p95/p99):
  - chat-long-context (A100): 18ms / 52ms / 120ms (baseline without paging: 14ms/36ms/65ms)
  - chat-long-context (L4): 26ms / 84ms / 210ms (baseline without paging: 18ms/48ms/92ms)

Observations / analysis:
1) Reuse vs workload: low reuse in chat-long-context (54% A100) driven by conversational prompts with high prefix variability. High reuse correlates strongly with higher throughput and lower evictions.
2) Eviction -> paging cascade: eviction spikes align with increased PCIe transfers and memory bandwidth bursts. Eviction of large KV slices triggers device->host moves (our current fallback paging) which cause stalls and bandwidth competition with inference kernels.
3) HW sensitivity: L4 nodes show much higher eviction and paging counts (factor ~2x-3x) due to lower device memory. Resulting latency penalty is worse on L4.
4) Migration overhead: when KV entries are paged back in, we observe serialization of requests in the runtime dispatcher for that shard leading to p99 amplification.
5) Kernel contention: bursts in memory bandwidth coincide with decreased kernel occupancy (Nsight traces show kernels waiting on memcpy completion).

Immediate hypotheses to validate:
- Our eviction policy (LRU-ish with chunk granularity = 64MB) is too coarse for conversational workloads; causes evicting recently reused KV slices.
- Paging path allocates host pinned memory and synchronous cudaMemcpy which blocks execution; switching to async pinned + overlapping could reduce stalls.

Proposed short-term mitigations (low risk, quick):
- Reduce eviction chunk size from 64MB -> 16MB and run AB test on chat-long-context (expected effect: 10-20% lower eviction rate, small CPU overhead).
- Increase KV prefetch threshold: do not evict slices if reuse score > 0.3 for last 5 requests (simple heuristic).
- Change paging memcpy to async + use CUDA streams to overlap with compute where possible (requires testing for correctness).

Longer-term changes (arch/algorithmic):
- Move from coarse LRU -> frequency-aware policy (LFU hybrid) that weights recent reuse and sequence position.
- Segmented caching: keep short-sequence prefixes pinned (hot segment) and cold segment evictable.
- Off-device persistent cache (NVMe-backed) with managed async prefetching tied to workload predictors; need infra support and careful SLOs.

Validation plan / experiments to run next:
- Run AB with chunk_size=16MB vs current 64MB on both A100 and L4 for 48h, capture same metrics.
- Implement async memcpy path and run microbenchmarks to measure memcpy overlap (target: 20-40% reduction in bandwidth-induced stalls).
- Add additional instrumentation: per-KV-slice timestamp of last access, reuse-count histogram, and track per-request stall time attributed to paging.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How does quantized KV memory layout affect chunking decisions (aligned boundaries may cause fragmentation)?
- How much CPU overhead / scheduling pressure will finer-grained eviction cause at high throughput?
- Is there a customer-visible correctness or determinism concern when switching to async prefetching and overlapping I/O?

Action items (owners):
- Mateo: implement chunk_size AB toggle + run 48h AB on testbed (due 2026-06-17).
- Priya: prototype async memcpy path and smoke test on L4 (due 2026-06-20).
- Owen: add per-slice reuse histogram instrumentation and dashboards (due 2026-06-14).
- Evelyn: synthesize results and recommend rollout plan (due 2026-06-22).

Notes / misc:
- Trace IDs: nsight-trace-chat-0609-1, perf-log-0609-2 (stored in S3: s3://redwood-infra/prof/nsight/0609/).
- Related tickets: INF-1482 (investigation), INF-1490 (eviction policy refactor).
- Quick experiment observation: reducing batch_size from 4 -> 2 on L4 reduced eviction rate by ~25% (workload dependent).

Next sync: quick tech-review + decision on chunk-size AB on 2026-06-11 11:00 PT (invite sent).

Notes to self: keep runs deterministic seeds, capture both device and host-side call stacks for eviction paths. Save raw nsight captures; they helped pinpoint memcpy-induced stalls in this run.
